# ABB: API Gateway Network Security Boundary

> **TOGAF Artifact Type:** Architecture Building Block (ABB)
> This document defines *what* an API gateway security boundary must be and do, expressed as architecture requirements, constraints, interfaces, and decisions. It is technology-platform-agnostic. For the AWS-specific realization of this ABB on Platform Gainwell, see [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md).

---
page_texts.3:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#1-motivation]

## 1. Motivation

APIs are the primary mechanism through which enterprise services are composed, integrated with partners, and exposed to consumers. In the absence of a dedicated network security boundary, backend services become directly reachable from external networks, susceptible to lateral movement within internal networks, and invisible to security monitoring — all of which are fundamentally incompatible with a Zero Trust architecture.

An **API Gateway Network Security Boundary** is an architectural element that intercepts, authenticates, authorizes, inspects, rate-limits, and logs all API traffic before it reaches any backend service. It replaces the perimeter-based DMZ model with an application-aware, identity-centric enforcement point aligned to NIST SP 800-207 and the enterprise Zero Trust reference architecture (GUID-SEC-ARCHITECTURE-VISION-0.0.01).

This ABB is necessitated by:

- **The elimination of the traditional DMZ** — Platform Gainwell uses no traditional demilitarized zone; application-layer controls at the API gateway serve as the cloud-native equivalent
- **The proliferation of APIs** — north-south (external) and east-west (internal) API traffic must both be governed; implicit trust within a network segment is never assumed
- **Regulatory obligations** — HIPAA §164.312(e), NIST SP 800-53 SC-7/SC-8, and ARC-AMPE (CMS v1.02, April 2025 — successor to MARS-E 2.0) mandate transmission security controls and audit trails for all API communication paths handling PHI/PII across ACA, Medicaid, and Partner Entities

---
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#2-concerns]

## 2. Concerns

This ABB addresses the following architectural concerns on behalf of its stakeholders:

| Concern | Stakeholder(s) | How This ABB Addresses It |
|---------|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Backend services must not be directly internet-accessible** | Security Architects, Network Architects | ABB requires all external API traffic to be mediated by the gateway; backend services are reachable only through the gateway's private network path |
| **All API traffic must be authenticated and authorized before reaching application logic** | Security Architects, Compliance Officers | ABB defines the gateway as a Policy Enforcement Point (PEP); no unauthenticated request may be forwarded to a backend |
| **PHI and PII must be encrypted in transit end-to-end** | Compliance Officers, Security Architects | ABB requires end-to-end TLS; gateway re-encryption of backend traffic is a hard constraint; cleartext backend hops are prohibited |
| **APIs must be protected against volumetric and application-layer abuse** | Security Operations, API Platform Owners | ABB requires rate limiting and application-layer threat filtering as first-class capabilities of the gateway |
| **All API traffic must be observable for security monitoring and compliance audit** | Security Operations, Compliance Officers | ABB requires tamper-evident, comprehensive access logging forwarded to a centralized security data lake |
| **Internal east-west API traffic must be as tightly controlled as external traffic** | Enterprise Architects, Security Architects | ABB applies the same authentication, authorization, and encryption requirements to internal APIs as to external ones |
| **Security controls must not be bypassable** | Security Architects | ABB requires deny-by-default backend access; any network path to backend services that bypasses the gateway violates a hard constraint |

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#3-architecture-requirements]

## 3. Architecture Requirements

The following requirements define what any realization of this ABB **shall** provide. These are technology-agnostic and must be satisfied by any Solution Building Block (SBB) that claims to realize this ABB.
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#31-boundary-enforcement]

### 3.1 Boundary Enforcement

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-01** | The gateway **shall** intercept 100% of API traffic for the workloads it protects; no direct network path from external clients to backend services shall exist | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-02** | Backend services **shall** be configured with deny-by-default network access controls; inbound traffic shall be permitted exclusively from the gateway's private network interface or load balancer | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-03** | Internal (east-west) API traffic **shall** be subject to the same authentication and authorization requirements as external (north-south) traffic; implicit intra-network trust is prohibited | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-04** | APIs not intended for external consumption **shall** be deployed on private, non-internet-routable gateway endpoints; public endpoints for internal-only APIs are prohibited | Must Have |
page_texts.7:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#32-encryption]

### 3.2 Encryption

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-05** | All client-to-gateway communication **shall** use TLS 1.2 as a minimum; TLS 1.3 is required as the preferred standard; TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are prohibited | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-06** | Gateway-to-backend communication **shall** be encrypted; cleartext (HTTP) connections from the gateway to backend services are prohibited for workloads processing PHI or PII | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-07** | Service-to-service authentication for east-west API traffic **shall** use mutual TLS (mTLS) with certificates issued by a trusted organizational certificate authority | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-08** | All cryptographic modules used for TLS enforcement **shall** meet FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validation requirements | Must Have |
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#33-authentication-and-authorization-zero-trust-pep]

### 3.3 Authentication and Authorization (Zero Trust PEP)

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-09** | Every inbound API request **shall** be authenticated against a verifiable identity credential (token, certificate, or signed request) before being forwarded to a backend | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-10** | The gateway **shall** enforce authorization decisions derived from a Policy Decision Point (PDP); authorization context shall include at minimum: consumer identity, requested resource, HTTP method, and data classification | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-11** | Cached authorization decisions **shall** expire; no authorization result shall be cached for longer than a configurable maximum that balances performance and revocation latency | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-12** | The gateway **shall** enforce access control policies derived from the least-privilege principle; only explicitly permitted consumers may invoke a given API endpoint | Must Have |
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#34-rate-limiting-and-abuse-prevention]

### 3.4 Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-13** | The gateway **shall** enforce rate limiting at the consumer, endpoint, and aggregate stage levels to prevent resource exhaustion of backend services | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-14** | Authentication and bulk-export endpoints **shall** have more restrictive rate limits than general read/write endpoints | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-15** | The gateway **shall** integrate with volumetric DDoS protection at the network layer; gateway-level throttling alone is not sufficient protection against large-scale attacks | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-16** | The gateway **shall** integrate application-layer threat filtering (equivalent to a Web Application Firewall) for all externally accessible API stages; this capability shall detect and block OWASP API Security Top 10 attacks | Must Have |
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#35-logging-and-observability]

### 3.5 Logging and Observability

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-17** | The gateway **shall** produce a tamper-evident access log for every API request, including at minimum: source identity, source network address, HTTP method, resource path, response status, response size, and timestamp | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-18** | Access logs **shall** be forwarded in near-real-time to the enterprise SIEM and retained for a minimum of 7 years to satisfy HIPAA §164.312(b) audit control requirements | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-19** | Access logs **shall not** contain raw request bodies, authorization credentials, or PHI data elements | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-20** | Gateway management-plane events (configuration changes, policy updates, stage deployments) **shall** be captured in a separate audit trail and forwarded to the enterprise SIEM | Must Have |
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#36-application-consumer-constraints]

### 3.6 Application Consumer Constraints

These requirements apply to the **application code and configuration artifacts** produced by teams that deploy APIs on top of this gateway boundary. They are not satisfiable by gateway infrastructure configuration alone. They apply to any SBB realizing this ABB regardless of the underlying technology platform.

> **Note on enforcement responsibility:** This section identifies the *concern domain* of the requirements (application-layer behavioral correctness), not the required implementing role. A realizing SBB may designate platform-owned automation components — such as a vended authorizer layer or opinionated Terraform module — to satisfy one or more of the requirements below. Where a platform component structurally satisfies a requirement independent of developer discipline, that is a valid and preferred realization. The realizing SBB must document, for each requirement in this section, whether compliance is delivered by platform infrastructure or by application-team artifacts, and what evidence is required under each path. See the AWS Platform Gainwell SBB (GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB §1.4 and §9.8) for the current platform automation component assignments.

| Req ID | Requirement | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **REQ-APIGW-21** | The authorization context forwarded by the gateway to the Policy Decision Point **shall** include a `dataClassification` field mapping the requested endpoint to the enterprise data sensitivity taxonomy (PHI, PII, Confidential, Public); this mapping **shall** be maintained in a current endpoint classification register | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-22** | Backend handlers that retrieve or modify resources addressed by an identifier (e.g., patient ID, claim ID, member ID) **shall** scope all data access operations to the authenticated principal propagated from the gateway authorizer context; unscoped queries that return records for any valid identifier are prohibited; for endpoints handling PHI or PII, this scoping constraint **shall** be enforced by a structural mechanism at the data access layer — such as database row-level security policies, a centralized authorization service evaluated on every query, or query construction that structurally excludes cross-principal records — that makes unauthorized cross-object access architecturally impossible; reliance on administrative review or code review alone does not satisfy this requirement for HIPAA-regulated data | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-23** | Where a single endpoint exposes operations at different privilege levels, the backend handler **shall** enforce a role-to-operation permission check against the principal's verified claims before executing the operation; gateway-layer endpoint authorization alone does not satisfy this requirement | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-24** | Every exception path in a gateway authorizer implementation **shall** terminate in a deny decision or a re-raised exception that the gateway converts to an authentication failure; no exception branch may short-circuit to an allow decision; dependency failures (identity provider unreachable, token validation service timeout) **shall** default to deny | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-25** | Authorization revocation checks **shall** fail closed: if the revocation store is unreachable the token **shall** be treated as revoked; in-memory revocation caches **shall** be bounded to a TTL strictly less than the authorizer cache TTL; scope reduction and role downgrade at the identity provider **shall** be treated as a revocation trigger | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-26** | The unique identity attribute emitted by a gateway authorizer into the access log **shall** unambiguously identify the individual or service principal making the request, sufficient for HIPAA §164.312(b) individual-level audit attribution; this attribute **shall** be populated on both allow and deny authorizer responses so that blocked access attempts are attributable; the specific field name and format is defined by the realizing SBB | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-27** | Authentication endpoints and bulk data export endpoints **shall** be declared in the endpoint classification register; their method-level rate limits **shall** be reviewed and confirmed as more restrictive than the default stage-level throttle before production promotion | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-28** | The gateway integration request configuration **shall** forward the gateway-assigned request correlation identifier as a header to the backend service; the backend service **shall** include this identifier in every request-scoped log entry to enable end-to-end incident reconstruction | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-29** | All integration response mapping templates and custom gateway error response bodies **shall** be reviewed before each production stage deployment to confirm that no PHI, PII, or authentication credential from a backend error response can appear in log-observable output; execution data tracing **shall** remain disabled on all production stages | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-30** | Certificate subject validation in gateway authorizer implementations handling mTLS traffic **shall** use exact string equality for CN and SAN comparisons; substring containment, prefix, or suffix matching is prohibited | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-31** | PHI and PII identifiers **shall not** appear in URL path segments or query parameters; sensitive identity and health data **shall** be transmitted only in the request body or request headers (over TLS); this applies to all HTTP methods, including GET requests that retrieve records identifiable by a PHI/PII key | Must Have |
| **REQ-APIGW-32** | Health-check, liveness, and management endpoints accessible on non-gateway network paths **shall** require explicit authentication or be restricted to a named network source; anonymous access to any management or diagnostic surface that bypasses the gateway is prohibited | Must Have |

> **Cross-reference — Input Schema Validation:** Requirements governing OpenAPI schema completeness, request model validation, and `additionalProperties` constraints are defined in [GUID-SEC-INT-API GATEWAY-2.8.01](GUID-SEC-INT-API%20GATEWAY-2.8.01.md). Application teams must satisfy that guidance alongside the constraints in this section.

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#ad-01-api-gateway-as-sole-network-ingress-point-no-dmz]

### AD-01: API Gateway as Sole Network Ingress Point (No DMZ)

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Context** | Traditional DMZ architectures use a network perimeter layer (firewalls, reverse proxies, load balancers) to protect backend services. Platform Gainwell is cloud-native; there is no physical network perimeter. The question is whether to recreate a DMZ pattern in the cloud or adopt a different model. |
| **Decision** | The API gateway **is** the network security boundary for API traffic. No DMZ layer is implemented. Backend services are isolated in private network segments accessible only through the gateway's private integration path. This is consistent with NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust principles and the Platform Gainwell Security Integration Strategy (STRAT-SEC-PLATFORM-001). |
| **Alternatives Considered** | (1) Cloud-native DMZ using separate VPC with firewall appliances — rejected due to complexity, cost, and incompatibility with Zero Trust principles; (2) No gateway, relying on network security groups alone — rejected as insufficient for application-layer enforcement. |
| **Consequences** | All backend services must be designed with gateway-mediated access in mind; any legacy service that requires direct internet access must be explicitly excepted and remediated — such services shall be tracked in a time-bounded remediation register; an exception without a scheduled remediation date is not valid. Gateway availability becomes a critical dependency for all API-exposed services. |
| **Standards** | NIST SP 800-207 §3.3, STRAT-SEC-PLATFORM-001 §2.2, §4.3 |

---
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#ad-02-end-to-end-tls-including-gateway-to-backend-re-encryption]

### AD-02: End-to-End TLS Including Gateway-to-Backend Re-Encryption

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Context** | TLS is widely implemented between clients and gateways. The question is whether TLS must also be enforced on the gateway-to-backend segment, which is inside a private network. Some architectures terminate TLS at the gateway and communicate with backends over cleartext, reasoning that private networks are trusted. |
| **Decision** | End-to-end TLS is required for the full request path: client → gateway **and** gateway → backend. Cleartext (HTTP) backend connections are prohibited for workloads processing PHI or PII. The Zero Trust principle of "assume breach" means private network segments are not treated as trusted; a compromised network segment must not expose PHI in cleartext. |
| **Alternatives Considered** | (1) TLS termination at gateway only, cleartext to backend — rejected due to HIPAA §164.312(e)(2)(ii) and Zero Trust incompatibility; (2) TLS termination at gateway only for low-sensitivity APIs — rejected to avoid a tiered policy that is operationally complex and easy to misconfigure. |
| **Consequences** | Backend services must be capable of serving HTTPS. Certificate management for backend services becomes an operational requirement. IaC pipelines must enforce HTTPS backend configuration and reject deployments with cleartext backend URIs. |
| **Standards** | HIPAA §164.312(e)(2)(ii), IETF RFC 8446, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8 |

---
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#ad-03-east-west-api-traffic-receives-the-same-controls-as-north-south]

### AD-03: East-West API Traffic Receives the Same Controls as North-South

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Context** | Internal service-to-service API calls are often treated as inherently trusted because they occur within a private network. This assumption breaks down in multi-tenant, multi-account, or microservices architectures where service compromise can enable lateral movement. |
| **Decision** | Internal (east-west) API traffic is subject to the same mandatory controls — authentication, authorization, encryption, rate limiting, and logging — as external (north-south) traffic. mTLS provides service identity verification for east-west calls. Private API gateway endpoints with access control policies enforce least-privilege between services. |
| **Alternatives Considered** | (1) Trust internal traffic; enforce controls only at perimeter — rejected as incompatible with Zero Trust and Assume Breach principles; (2) Separate, lighter-weight controls for internal traffic — rejected as operationally complex and creating inconsistency in the security posture. |
| **Consequences** | Service mesh or private gateway capabilities are required for east-west enforcement. All internal services must present verifiable identities (workload certificates or IAM roles). Certificate issuance and rotation for service identities is an operational dependency. |
| **Standards** | NIST SP 800-207 §2.1, GUID-SEC-ARCHITECTURE-VISION-0.0.01 |

---
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#ad-04-application-layer-threat-filtering-integrated-at-the-gateway]

### AD-04: Application-Layer Threat Filtering Integrated at the Gateway

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Context** | Network-layer controls (firewalls, security groups) operate at L3/L4 and cannot inspect HTTP/HTTPS application payloads. API-layer attacks such as injection, broken object-level authorization, and resource exhaustion require L7 inspection. The question is whether this inspection belongs at the API gateway or at a separate WAF appliance. |
| **Decision** | Application-layer threat filtering (WAF-equivalent capability) **shall** be integrated at or immediately adjacent to the API gateway for all externally accessible stages. It is a required capability of the gateway boundary, not an optional add-on. For externally accessible APIs, WAF integration is mandatory; for fully private internal APIs, network isolation provides the compensating control. |
| **Alternatives Considered** | (1) Separate WAF appliance upstream of the API gateway — acceptable but creates additional operational complexity; integration at the gateway layer preferred for cohesion; (2) Rely on API gateway request validation alone — rejected as insufficient against zero-day and complex injection patterns. |
| **Consequences** | WAF policy must be maintained alongside API definitions; as APIs evolve, WAF rules may require tuning. WAF false positive management becomes an ongoing operational responsibility. For HTTP API (v2) gateway types that do not support direct WAF attachment, a CDN layer with WAF must precede the gateway. |
| **Standards** | NIST SP 800-53 SC-7, SI-3, OWASP API Security Top 10 |

[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#5-provided-interfaces]

## 5. Provided Interfaces

This ABB exposes the following logical interfaces to consuming architectural elements. Realizing SBBs must implement all provided interfaces.

| Interface | Description | Consumer |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **AuthenticatedAPIProxy** | Receives inbound API requests, verifies caller identity, and forwards authenticated requests to the appropriate backend service | External clients, partner systems, internal services |
| **RateLimitedIngress** | Enforces per-consumer, per-endpoint, and per-stage request rate limits; returns standard error responses on limit breach | All API consumers |
| **ThreatFilteredIngress** | Inspects inbound requests for OWASP API Security Top 10 threats and blocks malicious payloads before they reach backend services | External API consumers |
| **AuditableTrafficLog** | Publishes a structured, tamper-evident access log record for every API request processed | SIEM, compliance audit systems, security data lake |
| **PolicyEnforcementPoint** | Enforces Zero Trust access control decisions for API traffic; decisions are derived from the enterprise Policy Decision Point (PDP) | Identity provider, authorization service |
| **PrivateBackendProxy** | Forwards authenticated, authorized requests to backend services via a private network path; no request reaches a backend without passing through the gateway | Backend application services, microservices |

---
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#6-required-interfaces]

## 6. Required Interfaces

This ABB depends on the following interfaces provided by other architectural elements. These are mandatory dependencies that any SBB realizing this ABB must satisfy.

| Interface | Provided By | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **IdentityVerification** | Enterprise Identity Provider (see GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01) | Validates bearer tokens, client certificates, or signed requests presented to the gateway |
| **PolicyDecisionPoint** | Authorization Service / Policy Engine | Provides access control decisions given identity claims and request context |
| **CertificateAuthority** | Enterprise PKI / Certificate Service | Issues TLS certificates for gateway custom domains and mTLS truststore |
| **PrivateNetworkPath** | Network Infrastructure (VPC, private subnet, routing) | Provides the private network segment over which the gateway communicates with backend services |
| **DDoSMitigation** | Network-layer DDoS protection service | Absorbs volumetric L3/L4 attack traffic before it reaches the gateway |
| **SIEMIngestor** | Enterprise SIEM Platform | Receives and indexes gateway access logs and management-plane audit events |
| **ApplicationThreatFilter** | WAF or equivalent (see GUID-SEC-NETWORK-WAF-2.2.02) | Provides OWASP-aligned application-layer threat detection and blocking for external API stages |
| **SecureDNSResolution** | Enterprise DNS (NIST SP 800-53 SC-20) | Resolves API gateway custom domain names to gateway endpoints; DNS must not resolve to backend IPs directly |

---
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#7-constraints]

## 7. Constraints

The following are hard architectural constraints. They are non-negotiable and cannot be overridden by a design decision at the SBB level without an architecture exception approved by the Security Architecture Advisory Group.

| ID | Constraint | Basis |
|----|-----------|-------|
| **CON-01** | Cleartext HTTP connections between the gateway and backend services are **prohibited** for any workload processing, storing, or transmitting PHI or PII | HIPAA §164.312(e)(2)(ii) |
| **CON-02** | TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are **prohibited** for any gateway endpoint | NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2, IETF RFC 8996 |
| **CON-03** | Any backend service protected by this ABB **shall not** have a network path to the internet that bypasses the gateway | NIST SP 800-207, NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 |
| **CON-04** | Access logs **shall not** contain PHI, PII, or authentication credentials | HIPAA §164.312(b); secondary exposure risk |
| **CON-05** | Authorization decision caching **shall not** persist beyond the configurable TTL maximum; stale cached decisions allowing access to revoked identities are a constraint violation | NIST SP 800-207 §2.2 |
| **CON-06** | APIs designated as internal-only **shall not** be reachable from public internet endpoints | NIST SP 800-53 SC-7, AC-4 |
| **CON-07** | All cryptographic modules used by the gateway **shall** be FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validated | FIPS 140-2/140-3 |
| **CON-08** | Access log retention **shall** be a minimum of 7 years for workloads subject to HIPAA | HIPAA §164.530(j) |

---
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#8-assumptions]

## 8. Assumptions

The following assumptions are made about the environment in which this ABB is deployed. If any assumption is invalidated, the affected architecture requirements and decisions must be re-evaluated.

| ID | Assumption |
|----|-----------|
| **ASM-01** | An enterprise identity provider capable of issuing and validating cryptographically verifiable identity credentials (tokens or certificates) is available and reachable by the gateway |
| **ASM-02** | Backend services can be configured to accept connections from only the gateway's private network path; they support HTTPS on their listening port |
| **ASM-03** | A private network segment exists that is not routable from the public internet, over which the gateway can communicate with backend services |
| **ASM-04** | An organizational certificate authority exists and can issue certificates for mTLS truststore configuration and backend TLS |
| **ASM-05** | A SIEM platform capable of ingesting structured gateway access logs in near-real-time is operational |
| **ASM-06** | DDoS mitigation capability is available at the network layer upstream of the gateway endpoint |
| **ASM-07** | The enterprise has defined data classification policies that can be applied to APIs (PHI, PII, Confidential, Public) to drive differential control application |

## 9. Instantiation Patterns

These patterns describe the abstract architectural topologies in which this ABB is instantiated. They are technology-agnostic; SBBs map these patterns to specific platforms and services.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#pattern-a--external-north-south-api-gateway]

### Pattern A — External (North-South) API Gateway

```
External Consumer (TLS)
  └─► [DNS / Custom Domain]
        └─► [API Gateway Security Boundary]  ← This ABB
              │  ├── Application Threat Filter (WAF)
              │  ├── Authenticator (Token / mTLS)
              │  ├── Rate Limiter
              │  └── Access Logger → SIEM
              └─► [Private Network Path]
                    └─► Backend Service (TLS, Private Subnet)
```

- **Use when:** API is accessible to external clients, partners, or mobile applications
- **Mandatory:** Application-layer threat filtering; end-to-end TLS; rate limiting; comprehensive access logging
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#pattern-b--internal-east-west-private-api-gateway]

### Pattern B — Internal (East-West) Private API Gateway

```
Internal Service A (mTLS)
  └─► [Private Endpoint / Access Control Policy]
        └─► [API Gateway Security Boundary]  ← This ABB
              │  ├── Service Identity Authenticator (mTLS / Workload IAM)
              │  ├── Authorization Policy Enforcer
              │  ├── Rate Limiter
              │  └── Access Logger → SIEM
              └─► [Private Network Path]
                    └─► Backend Service B (TLS, Private Subnet)
```

- **Use when:** API call is service-to-service within an internal trust boundary but lateral movement must be prevented
- **Application-layer threat filtering:** not required when compensating control (private endpoint + access policy) provides equivalent isolation
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-2.2.04.md#pattern-c--cross-boundary-api-gateway-multi-tenant-or-multi-account]

### Pattern C — Cross-Boundary API Gateway (Multi-Tenant or Multi-Account)

```
Consumer (Account / Domain A) (mTLS / Signed Request)
  └─► [Cross-Boundary Connectivity (PrivateLink / VPN / Direct Connect)]
        └─► [API Gateway Security Boundary]  ← This ABB
              │  ├── Principal/Organization Authenticator
              │  ├── Cross-Account Authorization Policy
              │  ├── Rate Limiter (per-tenant)
              │  └── Access Logger → SIEM
              └─► [Private Network Path]
                    └─► Shared Platform Service (TLS, Private Subnet)
```

- **Use when:** Shared platform services are consumed by workloads in different security domains, accounts, or organizations
- **Mandatory:** Principal-scoped authorization; per-tenant rate limiting and quotas; cross-boundary connectivity that does not traverse public internet

### 11.2 Infrastructure Assurance Evidence Requirements

Several controls in this ABB govern properties — network topology, cryptographic module certification, key management infrastructure, operational pipeline health, and log integrity — that are not observable by Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) or static Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) scanning alone. DAST probes API behavior from an external vantage point and cannot enumerate all network paths to backend services, confirm FIPS module certification, validate post-deployment log store immutability, or verify operational SIEM forwarding pipeline health. IaC SAST confirms declared configuration intent but cannot detect runtime drift or out-of-band mutations after deployment.

These controls require a separate **Infrastructure Assurance Track** aligned with NIST SP 800-53 CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring) and CA-2 (Control Assessments). Any SBB realizing this ABB **must** document how evidence for each of the following properties is produced, where it is stored, and at what frequency it is refreshed. The specific methods, tools, and procedures by which evidence is collected are within the scope of the realizing SBB, not this ABB.

| Control(s) | Evidence Property | Verification Track |
|---|---|---|
| **REQ-APIGW-01, CON-03** | Runtime backend network isolation is confirmed independent of IaC declarations; no path from any external network to any backend service exists that bypasses the gateway | Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM); Network Reachability Analysis |
| **REQ-APIGW-03** | East-west authorization, authentication, and encryption controls are enforced at runtime with the same effect as north-south controls | Internal Penetration Test (from within private network segment) |
| **REQ-APIGW-06, AD-02** | Gateway-to-backend communication uses encryption at runtime; runtime state matches IaC declarations and has not drifted through out-of-band changes | Configuration Drift Detection (continuous) |
| **REQ-APIGW-07** | The mTLS truststore accepts only certificates issued by the designated organizational certificate authority; no unauthorized or external CA roots are present | PKI / CA Hierarchy Audit |
| **REQ-APIGW-08, CON-07** | The cryptographic module performing TLS operations holds a current FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 validation certificate; FIPS mode is active at the platform layer | FIPS Module Certification Audit |
| **REQ-APIGW-11, CON-05** | Credentials revoked at the identity provider are rejected by the gateway within the configured TTL window; the revocation check is enforced at runtime, not only declared in configuration | Revocation Integration Test (CI/CD Pipeline) |
| **REQ-APIGW-15** | Network-layer volumetric DDoS protection is active, scoped to the gateway resource, and response escalation paths are operational | Infrastructure Subscription Audit |
| **REQ-APIGW-17** | The log archive is immutable; the storage layer enforces tamper-evident retention in a mode that cannot be overridden by any privileged administrative action | Storage Immutability Audit; Log Integrity Validation |
| **REQ-APIGW-18, CON-08** | The log forwarding pipeline is operational and delivers log entries to the SIEM within the expected latency; 7-year retention is enforced at the storage layer and has not been reduced through post-deployment configuration changes | SIEM Pipeline Health Test; Storage Retention Audit |
| **REQ-APIGW-19, CON-04** | Access logs produced at runtime contain no PHI, PII, or authentication credentials; this property holds across all code paths including error handlers and transformation functions | Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Scan on Log Archive; Application Code Review |
| **REQ-APIGW-20** | Management-plane events are captured in an operational audit trail and forwarded to the SIEM; the audit trail is active and current at the time of assessment, not only declared in configuration | Management Audit Trail Operational Test |

### Enterprise Architecture Principles Alignment

| EA Principle | How This ABB Instantiates It |
|-------------|------------------------------|
| **Zero Trust (Never Trust, Always Verify)** | Gateway as PEP: every request authenticated and authorized before forwarding, regardless of network location (AD-01, AD-03) |
| **Defense in Depth** | Gateway combines boundary isolation, authentication, application threat filtering, rate limiting, and logging into a layered control |
| **Least Privilege by Default** | Access control policies restrict which consumers may invoke which endpoints; deny-by-default backend network rules |
| **Encrypt Everything** | TLS 1.3 end-to-end including gateway-to-backend; mTLS for service identity (AD-02) |
| **Secure by Design** | Security controls are pre-conditions for API onboarding, not retrofitted; no API traffic is accepted before controls are validated |
| **Compliance as Code** | Gateway configurations realized in IaC; policy gates enforce security baseline before deployment |
